title: SLO-driven routing: architecture notes + incident play scripts
content:
Purpose and scope: This note documents an SLO-driven approach to routing and control-plane decisioning across multi-region deployments, and embeds compact, actionable incident play scripts for common and high-risk failure modes. It is intended for on-call platform engineers and architects who need a quick architecture reference plus immediate mitigation steps. High-level architecture summary (one-paragraph): - The routing layer is policy-driven: decisions are evaluated by a scoring engine that consumes real-time signals (latency percentiles, error rates, queue depth, capacity reports) and static constraints (region affinity, compliance tags, customer tier). A lightweight control plane coordinates steady-state policy distribution, leader election for topology changes, and sanity-checks before global rollouts. The data-plane (edge routers + region ingress) apply local short-circuit heuristics to preserve SLOs when central control becomes delayed. Design motivations and constraints: - SLO-first: routing heuristics must prioritize meeting per-customer latency and availability SLOs rather than optimizing for cost during emergencies. - Fail-open vs fail-safe: default is fail-open at the data-plane for read traffic (allow degraded capacity with throttling) and fail-safe for write/control operations (reject when consistency cannot be preserved). - Multi-region consistency: route decisions should be eventually consistent and monotonic during rollouts to avoid oscillation. - Observability: every decision is logged with a decision-id, policy-version, and contributing signals for post-incident analysis. Key components and signals (short): - Decision engine: policy-version, decision-id, route_score, reason_codes. - Health signals: rps, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, queue_depth, memory_pressure, gpu_util, kv_cache_hit_ratio. - Capacity signals: region_capacity_report, reserved_capacity_map, model_variant_capacity. - Safety knobs: circuit_breakers, rate_limit_overrides, emergency_fallback_rules, region_quarantine. Embedded run scripts / incident plays (compact, executable style): 1) Scenario: control-plane coordination leader election stall (control plane losing quorum) - Detection heuristics: - leader_heartbeat_missing > 30s AND >50% controllers reporting stale config_version - increase in policy_evaluation_errors at data-plane (>=5% of requests) - Immediate impact: route changes are delayed, new policy rollouts stall, but existing data-plane rules still apply. - Triage steps: 1. Alert owner (on-call platform lead) + add #platform-inc channel. 2. Check controller pods: kubectl -n controlplane get pods -l app=control-controller; kubectl logs for leader candidate. 3. Inspect etcd health: etcdctl --endpoints=$ETCD_ENDPOINT endpoint status; check majority and raft_leader. 4. If quorum lost, follow recovery path: try to bring back previously healthy controller nodes (start/scale) rather than force leader change. - Mitigation (fast): - If controllers are stuck in crashloop: scale replicas to 3 minimum, apply configuration rollback to last_known_good_policy_version (controlplane rollback tooling). - If etcd partitioned: identify network ACLs, restart failing etcd member with snapshot restore if necessary. - Validation: verify data-plane is still serving stable policies: curl -s "$EDGE/status?decision_version" and confirm decision_version == last_known_good. - Postmortem triggers: >10 minutes without auto-recovery or any customer-impacting errors. 2) Scenario: cross-region latency spike causing SLO breaches for a region (network degradation to region eu-west-1) - Detection heuristics: - p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for > 3 minutes combined with increased retry/backoff events. - Inter-region RTT > 150ms baseline and TCP retransmits elevated. - Immediate impact: requests routed into eu-west-1 show degraded user latencies and rising errors for stateful flows that depend on region-local caches. - Triage steps: 1. Verify provider region health (cloud status + BGP alerts). 2. Check egress/ingress network metrics at the region: net_errors, drops, queue lengths. 3. Pull per-customer SLO impact from dashboards and identify high-risk customers. - Mitigation (stepped): A) Soft reroute: adjust routing score to deprioritize eu-west-1 for non-bound traffic (set temporary weight=0.3) via controlplane patch: PATCH /policies/routing/{policy_id} body {"deprioritize_regions": ["eu-west-1"], "ttl": 15m}. B) For customers with strict region affinity, enable degraded local-mode: enable edge_local_cache_bypass=true so traffic avoids cross-region state lookups. C) If network continues to degrade, activate warm-standby region draining: mark eu-west-1 as quarantine and shift reserved capacity to eu-central-1 following the reserved_capacity_map. - Validation: compare p95s and SLO hit-rates after weight change; confirm error budgets stop burning for critical customers. - Rollback: after sustained healing for >= 30 minutes and normal RTTs, remove deprioritization and revert weight. 3) Scenario: model-variant capacity exhaustion in primary region during peak - Detection heuristics: - model_variant_capacity_utilization > 90% and provisioning queue growth > 200 req/s - increased inference tail-latency (p99) and SKIP responses due to OOMs - Immediate impact: higher latency + token drops for model-specific routes; customers see longer response times or failures. - Triage steps: 1. Review model_variant_capacity_map and shard distribution. 2. Inspect GPU telemetry and container OOM logs. 3. Check autoscaler logs and events for scale failures. - Mitigation (fast): - Activate model-fallback policy: route traffic to a compatible lower-cost/quantized variant with functional compatibility (policy rule: allow_variant_fallback=true). - Temporarily increase batch-size cap-down only if latency SLOs remain met for p95. - Move burst load to Dedicated capacity if customer has reserved capability. - Longer-term: expand dedicated pools or pre-warm variants by raising warm_pool_target for predicted peak windows. 4) Scenario: mis-deployed routing policy causing global oscillation (bad policy update) - Detection heuristics: - decision_version flapping between two versions in <5 minutes and route_score variance > 40% - sudden rise in routed_request_failures and 429s from token bucket exhaustion - Immediate impact: customers see repeated retries, increased cost from cross-region fails, and SLO violations. - Triage steps: 1. Identify policy version(s) from recent deployments: git tag, controlplane audit log. 2. If a canary rollout is in progress, halt further rollout (controlplane rollback command). - Mitigation (surgical): - Quick rollback to last_known_good_policy_version via controlplane: POST /controlplane/actions/rollback {"target_version": "v1234"}. - Place offending policy in quarantine and annotate with incident id. - If rollback fails, apply emergency circuit_breaker to route to regional defaults: set global_circuit_breaker=true. - Validation: ensure decision_version stabilized and route_score variance returns to normal. - Postmortem: capture decision logs, attach to JIRA-PLT-921 for analysis. 5) Scenario: partial data-plane outage in a single AZ within a region (node group scale failure) - Detection heuristics: - significant increase in client connections timed out for subset of edge nodes, node group unhealthy from cloud API - imbalance in active connections across nodes in same region - Immediate impact: localized client failures and increased latency for requests landing on affected AZ. - Triage steps: 1. Identify affected node group in cloud console and check recent instance events. 2. If autoscaler failed to replace nodes, trigger replacement via infrastructure automation. - Mitigation (immediate): - Rebalance: mark affected AZ nodes as draining in router; redistribute traffic to healthy AZs (set az_preference_score=0 for affected AZ). - If az imbalance persists, increase global burst capacity in other AZs for short window. - Validation: observe connection distribution and p95 per-AZ latency converging. Common recovery primitives (cheat-sheet): - Decision verification: curl $EDGE/decision?request_id=... to view decision payload; check reason_codes for 'safety:quarantine' or 'capacity:fallback'. - Force policy rollback: controlplane rollback --version --force (only after leader sign-off). - Quarantine region: controlplane regions quarantine add --ttl 15m --reason "network-spike". - Warm-standby shift: controlplane capacity shift --from --to --percent 50 --policy-id

. - Increase observability temporarily: ENABLE_DECISION_VERBOSE=1 and bump sampling to 100% for affected policy id. Operational guidance and guardrails: - Use incremental changes with short TTLs for emergency weight tweaks; prefer gradual ramp. - Always document emergency changes in the incident channel and create a controlplane change log entry (automated tooling will snapshot diff). - Do not change model fingerprints or quantization profiles during an active incident unless model correctness is not impacted. - For any rollback that affects >2% of traffic for >10 minutes, open an incident review and schedule a follow-up RCA. Post-incident checklist (short): - Reconcile policy versions and remove temporary TTLs. - Compare decision_logs pre/post incident and attach relevant slices to the ticket. - Update canary rules and add a regression test that simulates the observed signal combination. - If mitigation involved region shift, run capacity resync and warm_cache jobs to reduce cold-start impact. Open gaps and proposals (short bullet list): - Proposal A: implement a predictive signal that anticipates cross-region degradation by monitoring inter-region bandwidth trends and BGP changes; feed into decision engine to pre-warm backups. - Proposal B: add an automated safe-rollback that uses golden traffic replays for 2 minutes before committing a policy to 100%. - Proposal C: expand decision provenance with structured reasons to aid automated ML-based root-cause classification. Notes to reviewers: - This is intentionally compact: the goal is a single-page operational architecture + immediate play scripts for fast consumption on-call. Suggest we add short runbook links per scenario to Confluence for run-level detail. - TODO: attach runbook snippets with exact controlplane CLI commands and RBAC required for each action. End of doc.
